identification.summary: TA455 is the name used in ClearSky's November 2024 report on the 'Iranian Dream Job' campaign, in which an Iranian actor targeted the aerospace and defense sectors with fake job offers and deployed the SnailResin loader, which activates the SlugResin backdoor [S1][S2]. ClearSky and press coverage describe TA455 as a subgroup of Charming Kitten (APT35) [S2][S3]. The Hacker News reports that Google's Mandiant tracks TA455 as UNC1549 and PwC calls it Yellow Dev 13 [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Fake-job activity since at least September 2023, per The Hacker News summary of ClearSky [S2]. Mandiant dates UNC1549 activity to at least June 2022 [S4].
identification.notes: Cluster boundaries are unsettled. The record's relatedRecords note says MITRE lists Proofpoint's TA455 alongside UNC1549 under NIMBUS MANTICORE (G1059) and that Microsoft maps UNC1549 to Smoke Sandstorm; neither mapping was re-verified in this pass. Mandiant's February 2024 UNC1549 report assessed overlap with Tortoiseshell [S4], while ClearSky/The Hacker News place TA455 under Charming Kitten (APT35) [S2]; these placements differ and are not merged here.

attribution.sponsor: Iran (state sponsor not named by the cited sources at agency level). Mandiant assessed UNC1549 as Iran-nexus [S4]; ClearSky calls TA455 an Iranian actor [S1].
attribution.confidence: Mandiant attributed UNC1549 to Iran with moderate confidence in February 2024 [S4]. ClearSky concluded that Charming Kitten is either impersonating Lazarus to cover its tracks or has access to Lazarus methods and tools [S2]. Some antivirus engines flagged the malware as Kimsuky/Lazarus, so attribution is contested [S2].
attribution.basis: ClearSky analysis of lures, ZIP/DLL side-loading chain and overlap with North Korean Dream Job tradecraft [S2]; Mandiant technical reporting on UNC1549 [S4]. No government attribution was found in the sources gathered.

objectives: Espionage against aerospace, aviation and defense organizations and their staff, delivered through recruitment lures [S1][S2][S4]. Mandiant's 2025 reporting describes UNC1549 compromising Middle East aerospace, aviation and defense entities, with press describing a shift toward the global aerospace supply chain [S5].

targeting.notes: ClearSky describes defense-sector and aerospace targeting [S1][S2]. Regional detail comes from Mandiant's UNC1549 report [S4], which may not be the identical cluster to ClearSky's TA455 [S2]. A September 2025 report describes UNC1549 compromising 34 devices across 11 telecom organizations via LinkedIn job lures and MINIBIKE [S6].

capabilities.summary: ClearSky reports spear-phishing and fake recruiter lures delivering a ZIP archive containing an executable and a malicious secur32.dll (SnailResin) that is side-loaded and activates the SlugResin backdoor [S1][S2]. The Hacker News reports use of GitHub as a dead drop resolver to hide the real command-and-control server [S2]. Mandiant's UNC1549 reporting describes fake React-based career portals, Microsoft Azure infrastructure for C2, and the MINIBIKE and MINIBUS backdoors [S4], and later TWOSTROKE and DEEPROOT backdoors [S5]. Overlap of these toolsets with TA455's was not verified here.

diamond.adversary: Iranian actor tracked as TA455 (ClearSky), reported as a Charming Kitten subgroup and as UNC1549 by Mandiant and Yellow Dev 13 by PwC [S2]. Possible Lazarus imitation or tool access per ClearSky [S2].
diamond.capability: Fake recruiter lures, ZIP with side-loaded secur32.dll (SnailResin) loading the SlugResin backdoor, GitHub dead drop resolver [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Fake recruiting personas and sites, GitHub repositories used to hide C2 [S2]; Azure-hosted C2 and fake career portals in Mandiant's UNC1549 reporting [S4].
diamond.victim: Aerospace, aviation and defense personnel and organizations, chiefly in the Middle East [S1][S2][S4][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Iranian regional security competition is the likely context for Israel and UAE targeting; this is analyst inference and not stated in the cited sources.
diamond.technology: Exposure of staff to recruiter contact on professional networking and email, and ability to run unsigned archives and DLLs on endpoints [S2].

gaps: Could not open ClearSky's primary report (clearskysec.com/irdreamjob24) or the SecurityWeek, Infosecurity Magazine and RH-ISAC articles in this session; facts rely on search-result summaries and The Hacker News coverage [S1][S2][S3].
Proofpoint's own definition of TA455 was not found; whether ClearSky's TA455 equals Proofpoint's TA455, Mandiant UNC1549, MITRE NIMBUS MANTICORE and Microsoft Smoke Sandstorm is unverified.
Microsoft's description of SnailResin (a detection entry naming SlugResin as an update of BASSBREAKER) was seen only as a search result without date and was not cited.
Placement under Charming Kitten (ClearSky) versus Tortoiseshell overlap (Mandiant) is unreconciled.
Whether Lazarus imitation is deliberate or tooling is shared is unresolved.
The Cloudflare traffic-masking claim in the original record was not confirmed by gathered sources.
No government attribution or sanctions found; victim counts and data stolen are not public.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the aerospace and defense workforce reachable through professional networking sites, personal and corporate email, and endpoints that can unpack archives and load DLLs. STEP 2: The actor operates through social engineering of individuals rather than exploiting perimeter systems, so the human and recruitment channel is the operating environment. STEP 3: The pattern is a fake recruiter, then a ZIP with a signed-looking executable side-loading secur32.dll, then a backdoor with GitHub-hidden C2 [S1][S2]. The Lazarus-like tradecraft may complicate attribution [S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued job-lure espionage against Middle East and allied aerospace and defense staff and suppliers [S4][S5]. MDCOA is use of the same lure channel against US or coalition defense industrial base personnel to reach supply-chain data. Candidate indicators: unsolicited recruiter outreach to cleared or program staff, archives containing an EXE plus secur32.dll, outbound requests to GitHub from unusual processes, and Azure-hosted C2 [S2][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track vendor reporting under all aliases (TA455, UNC1549, Yellow Dev 13, Charming Kitten overlap) because naming is unsettled. (2) Authorities: monitoring of personal social media accounts of personnel is limited, so awareness training and reporting channels are the main levers. (3) Mission assurance: defense industrial base partners and contractors are the likely exposure; coordinate through DC3 and DIB cybersecurity channels. (4) Coordination: share indicators with allies in Israel and the Gulf, whose organizations appear most targeted [S4].
